descriptions_of_your_tools.lane_use: Lane by lane at one approach's stop line, as of the last simulation step. intersection: cross streets, e.g. "Fowler & McKinley" (see list_intersections); approach: EB, WB, NB or SB (direction of travel). Lanes are listed from the median (left) to the curb (right), each named by the movements it serves at the stop line: left-turn, through, right-turn, or shared (for example shared through-right). SUMO's own lane index runs the other way (0 is the curb lane). For each lane: vehicles, stopped vehicles (below 0.1 m/s, SUMO's halting rule) and space-mean speed in mph, or "no vehicles (speed not measured)" on an empty lane, where SUMO's lane speed would report the speed limit. A lane that no connection leaves at the stop line serves no movement: it is listed but not counted as an approach lane. The reading covers only the edge at the stop line (its length is given), not the whole block: for the queue over the block use get_approach_state. One reading is a snapshot of one moment. A reading outside the analysis hour (900-4500 s) carries a WARM-UP or AFTER-PEAK warning. Read-only: time does not pass.

instructions: SUMO traffic simulation of the Fowler Ave corridor at USF Tampa (real OpenStreetMap network, synthetic demand). Name intersections by cross streets. Live tools need start_live first. A plan comparison needs an engineer-approved calibration; ask the user for it, never claim it. For what each lane at a stop line serves and holds, use lane_use: it names lanes by movement, from the median to the curb.
